paper_summary: Aluminium matrix syntactic foams were made by stir casting Al-2014 alloy with 15, 20 and 25 vol% untreated fly ash cenospheres (60-90 um) and tested for dry sliding wear on a pin-on-disc tribometer (ASTM G99) at 5-25 N load and 4-8 m/s sliding velocity over 2000 m. Increasing cenosphere content lowered the specific wear rate and the friction coefficient (0.46-0.57 across the 15 runs), with the lowest wear at 25 vol%. A Gaussian Process Regression surrogate (training R2 = 0.9228, hold-out R2 = 0.8221) plus Sobol global sensitivity analysis showed cenosphere content (S1 = 0.4963) and applied load (S1 = 0.4752) dominate wear, while sliding velocity is almost irrelevant (S1 = 0.0257).

extraction_notes: This is a genuine hollow-particle (cenosphere) metal-matrix syntactic foam paper, but it reports ONLY tribological responses - friction coefficient, weight loss, wear rate and specific wear rate. None of these map to any field in the Properties schema, so every property field is null and the measured tribological numbers are recorded verbatim in test.specimen_notes for each of the 15 I-optimal design runs of Table 1. test_type is set to 'other' (dry sliding pin-on-disc); strain_rate_per_s is left null because sliding velocity (m/s) is not a strain rate. No mechanical properties (modulus, strength, density) and no measured foam density are reported anywhere in the paper. Cenosphere bulk density is given only as a range (0.6-0.9 g/cm3) and particle size only as a sieve range (60-90 um), so particle_true_density_g_cc and particle_mean_diameter_um are left null. Melt temperature is given as a range (750-800 C) so cure_or_process_temperature_c is left null. matrix_porosity_fraction uses the ImageJ-measured localized micro-porosity area fractions stated in Sec. 3.1 (<2.8% area for 20% FAC, 3.6% for 25% FAC); the paper states quantitative porosity measurement was not performed for the 15% composition, so it is null there. The 15%/20%/25% cenosphere contents are explicitly by volume, entered as fractions 0.15/0.20/0.25. Table 1 rows appear in the extracted text as one value per line; evidence quotes reproduce each row's values in column order. Values cited from other authors (Mehta et al., Zhang et al., Hussein and Eqal, Rugele et al., Doddamani et al.) in the Introduction/Discussion are literature comparisons for other material systems and were not extracted as records. GPR/Sobol results are model outputs about wear, not material properties, so they are summarised only.
